key_decisions: E2E-4.4 RE-PINNED IN PLACE (platform invariants — flagged for plan correction, done in behavior-specs.md §6 + phase-6 file with dated 2026-08-25 notes): the plan's literal 'Then' (the focused mid-draft survives the drop) is unreachable via ANY load trigger. Two invariants, both verified with in-page focusin/focusout + node-identity traces: (1) a drop event — trusted OR synthetic — moves focus (native drop focus semantics); (2) even a focus-preserving in-page load blurs the field, because decoding flips isReady → :disabled="!isReady" on #bpmInput, and a focused element that becomes disabled loses focus; the app's own commit-on-blur law (RD-1, @blur="commitBpmEntry") then commits the very draft W-16 protects. A live mid-draft therefore never reaches detection time. The re-pinned row asserts the reachable literal-step behavior: focused draft '9' + drop → blur-law commit (9 → clamped 30) → flag reset on load (CR §2.5 row 1) → prefill lands VISIBLY (field '120' + hint + announcement, stale clamp hint cleared). The no-clobber guarantee for a genuinely live mid-draft stays pinned at the P0 unit level (TD-U1.4/TD-U1.5, gate read at write time, R-10).

Prefill clears bpmClamped (beyond D-I's verbatim write list): the D-H cross-cutting claim 'the touched flag prevents suggestion + clamp-hint coexistence' was factually wrong — a clamped commit (flag true) followed by a re-drop (flag reset, row 1) lets the prefill land BESIDE the stale clamp hint (reproduced live in E2E debugging: both hints visible simultaneously). The prefilled value is in-range by clampBpm, so the clamp hint cannot describe it; the prefill write clears it. Pinned by TD-U1.1 (stale bpmClamped=true in the given state, cleared asserted); context.md D-H rationale corrected in place.

Ok-branch clears tempoSuggestion (beyond the phase file's change list): the hint is per-file data like waveformReady — a new file that detects null must not show the previous file's hint, which the phase's manual criterion 'drop the 3 s sine → no hint, no announcement, field untouched' requires after a suggestion is already shown. The plan never stated this clear; filled by the manual-acceptance reading and flagged in the phase map for Phase 7's docs (silence is per-file, W-13).

Barrel import of channelArrays/detectTempo in createMetronomadMethods.js per the phase pin (R-11 discipline): the barrel↔methods cycle is safe because the bindings are referenced only at call time and the barrel evaluates the Analysis modules before the App re-exports.

TD-U1.8/1.9 use real click-train buffers (90 BPM = TD-1.4 shape, 180 BPM = TD-1.5 shape — both pinned-positive detection outcomes), not the WF-I1 constant buffers: a constant buffer yields detectTempo null, which would make 'A's result writes nothing' vacuously true for the wrong reason. 90 vs 180 makes a guard failure (A's 90 leaking through) distinguishable from both the default (120) and B's result.

Negative E2E rows (E2E-4.3/4.4) cannot poll for ABSENCE node-side (the property holds from t=0 — the assertion would pass even if detection later misfired). watchForTempoSignals runs an in-page MutationObserver + 5 ms sweep for a bounded 500 ms window (dwarfs the <50 ms detection budget, PERF-1) and asserts the hint/announcement NEVER appeared while detection was resolving — with an initial check() covering a detection that finished before install.

withPinnedYields lifted from the WF-I1 describe callback to module scope (shared by WF-I1 + TD-U1 rows); TD-U1.1 mirrors the load's flag reset explicitly (vm._bpmTouchedThisFile = false) because a fresh never-loaded mock-VM has it undefined.
No commit made: the working tree carries uncommitted Phase 1–5 CR 001 work (user-managed); Phase 6 shares files with it. Flagged, per Phase 5 precedent.
learnings: NEW (not yet a learning doc — extends 2026-08-25-plan-pinned-ui-details-must-survive-platform-invariants.md): 'state persists across the trigger' is itself a platform invariant to check at test-construction time. A drop moves focus (native drop focus semantics — synthetic DragEvents included); and in this app any file load disables #bpmInput during decode (:disabled="!isReady"), so a focused field blurs and the RD-1 commit law commits the draft. Plan steps that assume focus/draft state SURVIVES a load trigger are unreachable — trace focus in-page (focusin/focusout + element-node identity via MutationObserver) before writing the assertion.

Filling in a previously no-op task in a pinned multi-task hook changes the pinned-yield QUEUE shape: the Phase-4 no-op tempo task never called setTimeout(0), so WF-I1.2/1.4's two-flush expectations silently broke when the real body (yield per task) landed. When a task count or yield count of _schedulePostLoadTasks changes, re-audit every flush-based test in the suite — the breakage surfaces as stale-passing tests in OTHER phases' rows.

For same-file re-drops, body[data-state]='ready' and canvas data-loaded='true' are ALREADY satisfied by the first load and cannot signal the second load's completion; the real signals are an actual state write that must change (E2E-4.2: the field value 140→120) or the ok-branch write that must clear (tempoSuggestion).

Announcement assertions must account for the load announcement: after a successful load the live region holds '<file> loaded', not '' — 'no tempo announcement' means 'still the load announcement' (two of my first RED drafts asserted '' and were test bugs, not app bugs).
